why: Top8 plain 427 decomposes as ~87.5% RL-like answers at ~91% accuracy plus ~12.5% plain-base answers at ~45%; the cue converts the plain-base share to cued-base quality and 1.5x strengthens the switch, giving about 0.875*0.915+0.125*0.88 of 500, roughly 455.

With the cue the 1.5x edit puts nearly every sample on the RL-like policy whose errors sit only on hard problems, so a vote over 4 adds about RL's own vote gain (+21 on a ~199 single mean), not the cued base's larger +33.
A cued 1.5x top8 sample is an RL-like answer at a weak-to-full RL dose, so its mean over 4 samples sits near RL's 200 per-sample mean, slightly below the selected 203 single draw.
